en.title: Transitive and intransitive verbs
en.summary: A transitive verb takes an object; an intransitive verb does not.

paragraphs: A transitive verb needs an object to complete its meaning. An intransitive verb does not take an object. To tell which one it is, ask what or whom after the verb. If there is an answer, the verb is transitive. Many English verbs can be both.

A dictionary marks the uses as vt or vi, or as T and I. Some verbs take two objects, an indirect object (a person) and a direct object (a thing): She gave him a gift. Intransitive verbs such as arrive, go and die cannot be made passive, because they have no object to move.

blocks.html:
TypeExample
transitiveHe opened the door.
intransitiveThe door opened.
two objectsI gave her a book.
transitive onlyShe likes tea.
intransitive onlyThey arrived.

paragraphs: Many verbs, such as open, break, burn, boil and change, can be transitive or intransitive with the same form. In the intransitive use the object of one sentence becomes the subject of the other: He broke the glass. The glass broke.
Some pairs differ in this way: rise (intransitive) and raise (transitive), lie (intransitive) and lay (transitive). We say The sun rises and She raises her hand.

items: Wrong: **He arrived the station.** Right: **He arrived at the station.**
Wrong: **The sun raises in the east.** Right: **The sun rises in the east.**

ro.title: Verbe tranzitive și intranzitive
ro.summary: Un verb tranzitiv poate avea un complement direct, iar un verb intranzitiv funcționează fără un complement direct.

paragraphs: Un verb tranzitiv poate avea un complement direct. Complementul direct răspunde la întrebarea „ce?” sau „pe cine?”. Un verb intranzitiv funcționează singur, fără un complement direct.

Verbele tranzitive cer un complement direct (substantiv sau pronume în cazul acuzativ). Verbele intranzitive exprimă de obicei o stare sau o mișcare. Unele verbe românești pot fi tranzitive sau intranzitive, în funcție de context.

blocks.html:
Tip de verbCaracteristicăExemplu
TranzitivComplement direct: „ce?”Noi **mâncăm** pâine proaspătă.
TranzitivComplement direct: „pe cine?”O **chem** pe Maria la masă.
IntranzitivExprimă o stareBunicul **doarme** acum în cameră.
IntranzitivExprimă o mișcareTrenul **pleacă** la ora două.
